arxiv-2004-13880.title: Bayesian Model Selection on Random Networks
arxiv-2004-13880.creator: Marios Papamichalis
arxiv-2004-13880.description: Abstract A general Bayesian framework for model selection on random network models regarding their features is considered. The goal is to develop a principle Bayesian model selection approach to compare different fittable, not necessarily nested, models for inference on those network realisations.

arxiv-2010-02984.title: MUSiC: a model-unspecific search for new physics in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2010-02984.description: Abstract Results of the Model Unspecific Search in CMS (MUSiC), using proton-proton collision data recorded at the LHC at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV , corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv , are presented. The MUSiC analysis searches for anomalies that could be signatures of physics beyond the standard model.

arxiv-2011-05812.title: Electrically-Reconfigurable Passive and Active Circuits in a Single Plasmonic Architecture
arxiv-2011-05812.creator: Charles Lin, Pohan Chang, Yiwen Su, Amr S Helmy
arxiv-2011-05812.description: Abstract Guided-wave plasmonic circuits are promising platforms for sensing, interconnection, and quantum applications in the sub-diffraction regime. Nonetheless, the loss-confinement trade-off remains a collective bottleneck for plasmonic-enhanced optical processes. Here, we report a unique plasmonic waveguide that can alleviate such trade-off and improve the efficiencies of plasmonic-based emission, light-matter-interaction, and detection simultaneously.

arxiv-2012-02322.title: A Laptop Ensemble Performance System using Recurrent Neural Networks Conference: NIME’20, July 21-25, 2020, Royal Birmingham Conservatoire, Birmingham City University, Birmingham, United Kingdom.
arxiv-2012-02322.creator: Rohan Proctor Charles Patrick Martin
arxiv-2012-02322.description: Abstract The popularity of applying machine learning techniques in musical domains has created an inherent availability of freely accessible pre-trained neural network (NN) models ready for use in creative applications. This work outlines the implementation of one such application in the form of an assistance tool designed for live improvisational performances by laptop ensembles.

arxiv-2106-06621.title: Piecewise-constant Neural ODEs
arxiv-2106-06621.creator: Sam Greydanus, Stefan Lee, Alan Fern
arxiv-2106-06621.description: Abstract Neural networks are a popular tool for modeling sequential data but they generally do not treat time as a continuous variable. Neural ODEs represent an important exception: they parameterize the time derivative of a hidden state with a neural network and then integrate over arbitrary amounts of time.

arxiv-2107-02480.title: Midwifery Learning and Forecasting: Predicting Content Demand with User-Generated Logs Conference: 2021 KDD Workshop on Applied Data Science for Healthcare; August 14–18, 2021; CCS: Forecasting Healthcare CCS: Neural Networks Deep Learning CCS: Time series User behavior
arxiv-2107-02480.creator: Anna Guitart, Ana Fernández del Río, África Periáñez, Lauren Bellhouse
arxiv-2107-02480.description: Abstract . Every day, 800 women and 6,700 newborns die from complications related to pregnancy or childbirth. A well-trained midwife can prevent most of these maternal and newborn deaths. Data science models together with logs generated by users of online learning applications for midwives can help to improve their learning competencies.

arxiv-2207-05936.title: Crystal and electronic structure of a quasi-two-dimensional semiconductor Mg 3 Si 2 Te 6
arxiv-2207-05936.creator: Chaoxin Huang, Benyuan Cheng, Yunwei Zhang, Long Jiang, Lisi Li, Mengwu Huo, Hui Liu, Xing Huang, Feixiang Liang, Lan Chen, Hualei Sun, Meng Wang
arxiv-2207-05936.description: Abstract We report the synthesis and characterization of a Si-based ternary semiconductor Mg 3 Si 2 Te 6 , which exhibits a quasi-two-dimensional structure, where the trigonal Mg 2 Si 2 Te 6 layers are separated by Mg ions. Ultraviolet-visible absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations were performed to investigate the electronic structure.

arxiv-2306-10673.title: Magneto-Optical Detection of the Orbital Hall Effect in Chromium
arxiv-2306-10673.creator: Igor Lyalin, Sanaz Alikhah, Marco Berritta, Peter M. Oppeneer, Roland K. Kawakami
arxiv-2306-10673.description: Abstract The orbital Hall effect has been theoretically predicted but its direct observation is a challenge. Here, we report the magneto-optical detection of current-induced orbital accumulation at the surface of a light 3 d d transition metal, Cr. The orbital polarization is in-plane, transverse to the current direction, and scales linearly with current density, consistent with the orbital Hall effect.

arxiv-2311-15335.title: TORE: Token Recycling in Vision Transformers for Efficient Active Visual Exploration
arxiv-2311-15335.creator: Jan Olszewski, Dawid Rymarczyk, Piotr Wójcik, Mateusz Pach, Bartosz Zieliński
arxiv-2311-15335.description: Abstract Active Visual Exploration (AVE) optimizes the utilization of robotic resources in real-world scenarios by sequentially selecting the most informative observations. However, modern methods require a high computational budget due to processing the same observations multiple times through the autoencoder transformers. As a remedy, we introduce a novel approach to AVE called TOken REcycling (TORE).

arxiv-2312-12346.title: The mod 2 2 cohomology rings of the alternating subgroups of the Coxeter groups of Type B \Bgroup Thanks: The first author acknowledges the MIUR Excellence Department Project awarded to the Department of Mathematics, University of Rome Tor Vergata, CUP E83C18000100006.
arxiv-2312-12346.creator: Lorenzo Guerra, Santanil Jana
arxiv-2312-12346.description: Abstract . We show that the direct sum of the cohomology groups of the alternating subgroups of the family of Coxeter groups of Type B B exhibits an almost-Hopf ring structure. We apply techniques developed by Giusti and Sinha to fully compute a presentation of this structure for mod 2 2 coefficient.

arxiv-2406-07366.title: Fast and accurate evaluation of Biot–Savart integrals over spatial curves in periodic domains
arxiv-2406-07366.creator: Juan Ignacio Polanco
arxiv-2406-07366.description: Abstract The Biot–Savart law is relevant in physical contexts including electromagnetism and fluid dynamics. In the latter case, when the rotation of a fluid is confined to a set of very thin vortex filaments, this law describes the velocity field induced by the spatial arrangement of these objects.

arxiv-2407-08461.title: Fractional Brownian motion in confining potentials: non-equilibrium distribution tails and optimal fluctuations
arxiv-2407-08461.creator: Baruch Meerson, Pavel V. Sasorov
arxiv-2407-08461.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Baruch Meerson, Pavel V. Sasorov. At long times, a fractional Brownian particle in a confining external potential reaches a non-equilibrium (non-Boltzmann) steady state. Here we consider scale-invariant power-law potentials V ⁡ ( x ) ∼ | x | m V(x)\sim|x|^{m} , where m > 0 m>0 , and employ the optimal fluctuation method (OFM) to determine the large- | x | |x| tails of the steady-state probability distribution 𝒫 ⁡ ( x ) \mathcal{P}(x) of the particle position.

arxiv-2407-11926.title: Far from Perfect: Quantum Error Correction with (Hyperinvariant) Evenbly Codes
arxiv-2407-11926.creator: Matthew Steinberg, Junyu Fan, Robert J. Harris, David Elkouss, Sebastian Feld, Alexander Jahn
arxiv-2407-11926.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Matthew Steinberg, Junyu Fan, Robert J. Harris, David Elkouss, Sebastian Feld, Alexander Jahn. We introduce a new class of qubit codes that we call Evenbly codes, building on a previous proposal of hyperinvariant tensor networks. Its tensor network description consists of local, non-perfect tensors describing CSS codes interspersed with Hadamard gates, placed on a hyperbolic { p , q } \{p,q\} geometry with even q ≥ 4 q\geq 4 , yielding an infinitely large class of subsystem codes.

arxiv-2505-24495.title: Convexity of the Berezin range of operators on ℋ γ ​ ( 𝔻 ) \mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(\mathbb{D}) Thanks: Dr. Satyajit Sahoo is thankful to IIT Bhubaneswar for providing the necessary facilities to carry out this work.
arxiv-2505-24495.creator: Sandip Kumar Maiti, Satyajit Sahoo, Gorachand Chakraborty
arxiv-2505-24495.description: Abstract . In this paper, we characterize the convexity of the Berezin range for finite-rank operators acting on the weighted Hardy space ℋ γ ​ ( 𝔻 ) \mathcal{H}_{\gamma}(\mathbb{D}) over the unit disc 𝔻 \mathbb{D} . We provide a complete classification in terms of convexity for concrete operators.

arxiv-2509-05292.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Ranking Utility Tuning in the Ad Recommender System at Pinterest DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Information systems Online advertising CCS: Computing methodologies Reinforcement learning
arxiv-2509-05292.creator: Xiao Yang, Mehdi Ben Ayed, Longyu Zhao, Fan Zhou, Yuchen Shen, Abe Engle, Jinfeng Zhuang, Ling Leng, Jiajing Xu, Charles Rosenberg, Prathibha Deshikachar
arxiv-2509-05292.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xiao Yang, Mehdi Ben Ayed, Longyu Zhao, Fan Zhou, Yuchen Shen, Abe Engle, Jinfeng Zhuang, Ling Leng, Jiajing Xu, Charles Rosenberg, Prathibha Deshikachar. The ranking utility function in an ad recommender system, which linearly combines predictions of various business goals, plays a central role in balancing values across the platform, advertisers, and users.

arxiv-2510-19053.title: Invariant Theory Beyond Reductivity: Hilbert and Schwarz Theorems for Discrete Lorentz and Cocompact Groups Email address: leandro.oliveira@ufscar.br
arxiv-2510-19053.creator: Leandro Nery
arxiv-2510-19053.description: Abstract Classical invariant theory provides a complete framework for reductive and compact Lie groups, but the non-reductive and non-compact cases are significantly more complex and less completely understood. This work investigates two distinct regimes: discrete subgroups of the Lorentz group O(n,1) acting on ℝ n , 1 \mathbb{R}^{n,1} , and cocompact actions of discrete groups on ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} .

arxiv-2601-05130.title: Sparsity and uniform regularity for regularised optimal transport Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author
arxiv-2601-05130.creator: Rishabh S. Gvalani ∗, Lukas Koch
arxiv-2601-05130.description: Abstract . We consider regularised quadratic optimal transport with subquadratic polynomial or entropic regularisation. In both cases, we prove interior Lipschitz-estimates on a transport-like map and interior gradient Lipschitz-estimates on the potentials, under the assumption that the transport map solving the unregularised problem is bi- C 1 , α C^{1,\alpha} -regular.

pmc-10588667.title: Maternal supplementation with Limosilactobacillus reuteri FN041 for preventing infants with atopic dermatitis: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-10588667.creator: Renqiang Yu, Yizhe Ma, Zichen Luo, Ce Qi, Anni Xie, Yifan Jiang, Baoli Zhu, Jin Sun
pmc-10588667.description: BackgroundAtopic dermatitis (AD) has increased rapidly with rapid urbanization; however, the treatment options for AD are lacking because the commonly used therapies can only alleviate symptoms. Limosilactobacillus reuteri (L. reuteri), FN041 is a specific strain isolated from human breast milk, and its protective potential against AD has been confirmed.

pmc-10594756.title: Double-wire technique to facilitate vein of Marshall cannulation and ethanol infusion in atrial fibrillation: a case series
pmc-10594756.creator: Hong-Da Zhang, Lei Ding, Kuo Zhang, Feng-Yuan Yu, Li-Jie Mi, Si-Xian Weng, Zi-Han Jiang, Min Tang
pmc-10594756.description: BackgroundThe vein of Marshall (VOM) ethanol infusion is increasingly performed in combination with catheter ablation in atrial fibrillation (AF). The cannulation of the VOM can sometimes be challenging. This study aimed to evaluate the double-wire technique in cases of difficult cannulation of the VOM.Case presentationPatients with AF scheduled for combined catheter ablation and VOM ethanol infusion were consecutively enrolled.

pmc-11398038.title: A Crowdsourced AI Framework for Atrial Fibrillation Detection in Apple Watch and Kardia Mobile ECGs
pmc-11398038.creator: Ali Bahrami Rad, Miguel Kirsch, Qiao Li, Joel Xue, Reza Sameni, Dave Albert, Gari D. Clifford
pmc-11398038.description: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AFib) detection via mobile ECG devices is promising, but algorithms often struggle to generalize across diverse datasets and platforms, limiting their real-world applicability. Objective: This study aims to develop a robust, generalizable AFib detection approach for mobile ECG devices using crowdsourced algorithms.

pmc-11539666.title: Prediction of menstrual recovery patterns in premenopausal women with breast cancer taking tamoxifen after chemotherapy: an ASTRRA Substudy
pmc-11539666.creator: Young Joo Lee, Woo Chul Noh, Sungchan Gwark, Hyun-Ah Kim, Jai Min Ryu, Seung Il Kim, Eun-Gyeong Lee, Seock-Ah Im, Yongsik Jung, Min Ho Park, Kyong Hwa Park, Su Hwan Kang, Joon Jeong, Eunhwa Park, Sung Yong Kim, Min Hyuk Lee, Lee Su Kim, Woosung Lim, Seonok Kim, Hee Jeong Kim
pmc-11539666.description: BackgroundChemo-endocrine therapy can lead to various side effects associated with ovarian dysfunction. Predicting menstrual recovery is necessary to discuss the treatment-related issues regarding fertility and premature menopause with patients.MethodsIn the ASTRRA trial, patients who resumed ovarian function within 2 years after chemotherapy were randomized to receive tamoxifen for 5 years or OFS with tamoxifen for 2 years.

pmc-12345202.title: Towards engineering agaricomycete fungi for terpenoid production
pmc-12345202.creator: Riccardo Iacovelli, Dominik Mojzita, Peter Richard, Yvonne Nygård
pmc-12345202.description: Since ancient times, humans have harnessed the vast metabolic abilities of fungi to produce food, beverages, and medicines. Biotechnology and genetic engineering have opened new avenues to tailor and enhance these abilities, transforming fungi into powerful industrial workhorses.In this minireview, we focus on the biotechnological potential of Agaricomycetes, a class of basidiomycete fungi that includes the so-called 'true' mushrooms.

pmc-13394667.creator: Yijia Wang, Xing Feng, Shuhui Zhao, Yuchong Fu, Ao Zhang, Xiaofeng Shen, Bowen Yu, Yihao Wang, Jiahui Lin, Bing Zhang, Weiping Ji, Lianpin Wu, Xiaoling Guo

pmc-13488458.title: Structure and conformational dynamics of the Pseudomonas CbrA transceptor
pmc-13488458.creator: Melanie A. Orlando, Tejas Shah, Matthew W. Faber, Samik Bose, Benjamin J. Orlando
pmc-13488458.description: The CbrA protein is a central regulator of carbon metabolism, biofilm formation, and virulence in Pseudomonas species, but the molecular mechanisms by which CbrA links nutrient sensing to downstream signaling has remained unclear. CbrA is a rare “transceptor” that combines membrane transporter and histidine kinase domains into a single functional polypeptide.

pmc-13587306.title: Co-occurrence of triple ESBL-associated genes (blaCTX−M, blaTEM and blaSHV) in Gram-negative bacteria from clinical specimens at a provincial hospital in Far-Western Nepal
pmc-13587306.creator: Madan Singh Bohara, Supriya Sharma, Dwij Raj Bhatta
pmc-13587306.description: BackgroundAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) among Gram-negative bacteria, particularly those producing extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBLs), represents a significant global healthcare challenge. CTX-M enzymes have achieved global dominance, often disseminated through plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer, complicating treatment in resource-limited settings. This study aimed to determine prevalence, antimicrobial resistance patterns and ESBL-associated gene profiles in clinical Gram-negative isolates.
